The identity-by-property-adherence primitive asserts that an entity's classification depends entirely on its instantiation of a kind's defining features. Misalignment triggers a correction protocol: either revise the entity's category, redefine the kind, or acknowledge a change in the entity itself. The logical correction principle enforces that such corrections must align with the underlying logical architecture—empirical anomalies do not invalidate the system but prompt recalibration of individual instances.
